Grapes in India at a Glance & Export Traceability

Direct Answer · Grape Farming in India

India cultivates roughly 1.62 lakh hectares (162,000 ha) of grapes producing 3.7 million MT (21–23 t/ha), with ~95% in Maharashtra (Nashik, Sangli, Solapur, Pune) and Karnataka (Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Belagavi, Bengaluru). In 2025–26, India exported 2.24 lakh tonnes (US$ 368 million) to 46 countries via mandatory APEDA GrapeNet [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA 2026].

Rule 1 · Rootstock

Pick by Water Sodium, Not Blindly Dogridge

ICAR-NRCG Pune proved Dogridge cannot exclude Sodium (Na⁺) — saline borewells cause K deficiency and Year 4–5 dead cordons. Use 110R or B2-56 in saline/drought soils.

Compare 6 rootstocks →
Rule 2 · Pruning

Apr 31–60 DAP & 48-Hr Dormex Lock

Fruit-bud differentiation happens 35–60 days after April pruning (hard-cut N!). After October pruning (5–10 buds), apply Dormex 50% SL (30–40 ml/L) within 24–48 hrs.

View pruning calendar →
Rule 3 · EU MRL Safety

Avoid CCC, Late Phosphonates & >2 ppm CPPU

EU export rejections spike from Chlormequat Chloride (CCC), Fosetyl-Al, Mancozeb, Carbendazim, and >2 ppm CPPU. Always obey current-season ICAR-NRCG Annexure-5 PHIs.

Interactive Crop-Stage Stepper (April Foundation → October Harvest)

Tap any pruning or fruiting stage to check exact DAP window, daily drip water (L/vine/day), fertigation focus, canopy task, and EU MRL/disease alerts [ICAR-NRCG].

April Foundation Pruning & Shoot Flush

Apr 0–30 DAP
Daily Drip Water
6–10 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
Basal 40–50 t/ha FYM + 30% annual P (SSP); 25% N + 10% P + 10% K via Urea + 19:19:19 / MAP
Canopy & PGR Task
Back-prune to 0–2 basal buds, strip loose trunk bark, thin shoots at 15–30 DAP to 30–40 uniform shoots/vine.
Top Stage Alert: Flea Beetle (Udadya) & Anthracnose Alert Inspect swollen buds for Flea Beetle (>5/vine ETL). Strip bark pre-pruning and protect young shoots against Anthracnose with Copper (2–2.5 g/L) [ICAR-NRCG].
Open full guide for this stage →

Fruit-Bud Differentiation Window (Critical)

Apr 31–60 DAP
Daily Drip Water
8–12 L / vine / day (NO drought stress!)
Nutrient Focus
HARD N-BRAKE (5% N only!) + 15% P + 10% K via MKP (0:52:34) + SOP (0:0:50). Collect 45 DAP petiole sample.
Canopy & PGR Task
Pinch sub-canes mechanically at 5–7 leaves + 6-BA (10 ppm) / Uracil (50 ppm). Keep Y-trellis open for summer sunlight on basal buds.
Top Stage Alert: Excess N or CCC MRL Trap Excess Nitrogen or canopy shade during Days 31–60 turns fruit buds into blind tendrils. Avoid repeated Chlormequat Chloride (CCC/Lihocin) sprays — top EU MRL failure trigger [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA].
Open full guide for this stage →

Monsoon Cane Ripening & Wood Hardening

Apr 61–120 DAP
Daily Drip Water
Rainfed / 4–8 L / vine / day in dry spells
Nutrient Focus
5% N + 0% P + 10% K via SOP (0:0:50) + MgSO4 / Boron check to ripen 8–10 mm brown canes.
Canopy & PGR Task
Maintain 30°–40° Extended Y-Trellis airflow; remove excess water shoots and diseased monsoon foliage.
Top Stage Alert: Monsoon Downy Mildew & Arm Dieback Protect cane leaves from Downy Mildew (Kevda) with Bordeaux (0.5–1%) / Copper so carbohydrates store properly. Paste trunk pruning wounds with Copper oxychloride against Botryosphaeria dieback [ICAR-NRCG].
Open full guide for this stage →

October Forward Pruning, Dormex & Bloom

Oct 1–40 DAP
Daily Drip Water
6–10 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
25% N + 35% P + 15% K via MAP (12:61:00) + Urea. Pre-bloom 0.1% B + 0.25% Zn prevents shot berries.
Canopy & PGR Task
Test bud fruitfulness under microscope; prune 5–10 buds; apply Dormex 50% SL (30–40 ml/L) WITHIN 24–48 hrs. Apply GA3 10 ppm pre-bloom (pH 5.5–6.0).
Top Stage Alert: 48-Hr Dormex Deadline & Wet-Panicle Downy Mildew Waiting past 48 hrs after pruning ruins uniform sprouting. Unseasonal Oct rain causes tendril reversion ("fillage") and explosive Downy Mildew — rotate FRAC groups immediately [ICAR-NRCG].
Open full guide for this stage →

Capfall Thinning, Fruit Set & 6 mm Stage

Oct 41–70 DAP
Daily Drip Water
10–14 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
25% N + 10% P + 20% K + Calcium Nitrate (TANK B ONLY!) + KNO3 (13:0:45) + SOP. Collect Oct full-bloom petioles.
Canopy & PGR Task
Capfall GA3 15–20 ppm (50% & 90% capfall); balance load to 35–40 bunches/vine; scissor-thin berries to 80–100/bunch.
Top Stage Alert: Thrips Scab & Tank A/B Lock Thrips (>5/shoot) scar 3–6 mm berries with corky russet rings — hang blue sticky traps (25/ha) and rotate Spinosad/Emamectin per Annexure-5 PHI. Never mix Ca(NO3)2 with SO4/PO4.
Open full guide for this stage →

Berry Sizing & EU-Safe GA3/CPPU Dip

Oct 71–105 DAP
Daily Drip Water
14–22 L / vine / day (Peak demand)
Nutrient Focus
15% N + 0% P + 25% K via KNO3 + SOP + MgSO4. STOP ALL NITROGEN BY 95–105 DAP!
Canopy & PGR Task
Berry dip at 3–4 mm & 6–7 mm: GA3 30–40 ppm OR GA3 25–30 ppm + CPPU 1–2 ppm strictly ONCE. Skirt bunches / apply bags.
Top Stage Alert: Never Exceed 2 ppm CPPU & Stop Mancozeb/Phosphonates Early CPPU >2 ppm causes thick crunchy skin, <16°Brix, berry shatter & EU MRL violation. Release Cryptolaemus (1,500–2,500/ha) for mealybugs; halt Fosetyl-Al & Mancozeb per NRCG Annexure-5 PHI.
Open full guide for this stage →

Veraison, Sugar Build & GrapeNet Harvest

Oct 106–150 DAP
Daily Drip Water
8–12 L / vine / day (Taper 7–10 d pre-harvest)
Nutrient Focus
0% N + 0% P + 10–15% K via SOP (0:0:50) ONLY to build >=16°Brix & firm pedicels.
Canopy & PGR Task
Check NRL-NRCG residue clearance 15–20 d pre-pick. Harvest >=16°Brix (~20:1 sugar/acid, 16–18 mm) for EU export or 22–24°Brix for Sangli raisins.
Top Stage Alert: Pink Berry, Cracking & Cold-Chain Rule Irregular veraison drip triggers berry cracking. Shade exposed clusters against Pink Berry. Pre-cool export cartons (4.5–5 kg + SO2 pad) within 4–6 hrs to 0–1°C (90–95% RH) [APEDA 2026].

Quick Field Look-Alike Triage (Most Confused Vineyard Symptoms)

Direct Answer · Field Look-Alike Diagnosis

Misdiagnosing Downy Mildew (Kevda) as Powdery Mildew (Bhuri) or blaming fungus for Dogridge Sodium scorch wastes critical spray windows. Verify upper oil spots vs ash-grey dust, check wood cross-sections for Botryosphaeria wedges, and confirm petiole Na⁺/Cl⁻ before applying chemical fixes [ICAR-NRCG].

Fungal Leaf & Bunch Triage
CURABLE · ACT IN <24 HRS

Downy Mildew (Kevda)

Plasmopara viticola
  • Translucent yellow "oil spots" on UPPER leaf surface
  • Fluffy white cottony spore growth strictly on LOWER surface
  • Wet Oct rain turns entire young flower panicle brown/twisted
Field Fix: Strip low shaded leaves; rotate Copper (2 g/L), Dimethomorph (1 g/L) + Mancozeb, Mandipropamid, or Cymoxanil+Mancozeb. Stop Phosphonates & Mancozeb early for EU MRL PHI [ICAR-NRCG].
CURABLE · DRY WEATHER

Powdery Mildew (Bhuri)

Erysiphe necator
  • Ash-grey dusty powder on BOTH leaf surfaces & green canes
  • Floury grey coating on berries -> scarred skin -> vertical berry cracking
  • Thrives in dry, warm, shaded Y-trellis/Bower interiors
Field Fix: Pull cluster-zone leaves for airflow; Wettable Sulphur (2 g/L — stop above 32–35°C!), rotate Myclobutanil (0.4 g/L), Azoxystrobin, or Potassium bicarbonate near harvest [ICAR-NRCG].
Vine Decline & Cordon Death Triage
MANAGEABLE · SWITCH TO 110R

Dogridge Na+ Toxicity / K-Mg Scorch

Saline Water (ECw >1.0 dS/m, Na+)
  • Marginal leaf scorching + interveinal yellowing on older leaves
  • Petiole test shows Na >0.40–0.50% or Cl >1.0–1.5% alongside low K/Mg
  • Gradual cordon weakening in Year 4–5 on Dogridge under saline borewells
Field Fix: Auto-block MOP immediately; switch to SOP (0:0:50) + 0.5–1% MgSO4 + gypsum + 10–15 t/ha mulch + water pH 6.5 acidification. Replant saline blocks on 110R / B2-56 [ICAR-NRCG].
NO SYSTEMIC CURE · PRUNE WOOD

Arm Dieback / Trunk Canker

Botryosphaeria spp.
  • Sudden wilting/death of one entire spur, arm, or cordon
  • Cross-section cut of wood shows dark brown wedge-shaped necrosis
  • Often enters through unprotected April/October pruning cuts
Field Fix: Cut back ruthlessly until cross-section shows 100% clean white-green wood. Immediately seal every cut with Copper oxychloride / Bordeaux wound paste + Trichoderma [ICAR-NRCG].

State-by-State Priorities & Multilingual Vineyard Glossary

Direct Answer · Regional Grape Priorities

Maharashtra (~70% share) prioritizes 110R salinity shifts, Oct-rain Downy Mildew, and CCC/Phosphonate EU MRL compliance; Karnataka (~25%) focuses on Vijayapura raisin hygiene, alkaline black-soil K/Mg, and Bangalore Blue anthracnose; Tamil Nadu and AP/Telangana manage high-K double-crop Bowers, Powdery Mildew, and Thrips [ICAR-NRCG; IIHR; TNAU].

Top Indian Grape Grower Questions (FAQs)

Why should Indian grape growers choose 110R rootstock over Dogridge in saline borewell water?

ICAR-NRCG Pune proved Dogridge cannot exclude Sodium (Na+); under saline water it accumulates Na+, triggers Potassium/Magnesium deficiency, and causes dead cordons after Year 4–5. 110R (or NRCG clone B2-56) actively excludes Na+ and sustains fruitfulness and Brix.

What are the safe irrigation water salinity (ECw), chloride, and bicarbonate limits for grapes?

Excellent grape water has ECw < 1.0 dS/m (above 2.7 dS/m causes severe yield loss) and Chloride <= 3 me/L on own-rooted vines (up to 18 me/L on tolerant rootstocks). If bicarbonates exceed 2.5–3.0 me/L, acidify drip water with controlled H2SO4 to pH 6.5 [ICAR-NRCG; MANAGE].

What is double pruning and single cropping in Indian vineyards?

In Maharashtra and Karnataka, vines undergo April (Foundation) pruning to 0–2 basal buds to build sunlit canes where fruit-bud differentiation occurs at 35–60 DAP, followed by October (Forward) pruning to 5–10 buds for a single Jan–Apr harvest (120–160 DAP) [ICAR-NRCG; MPKV].

How many Gunthas equal 1 Acre in Maharashtra and Gujarat grape belts?

1 Acre equals exactly 40 Gunthas (4,046.86 m², or 101.17 m² per Guntha). Regional Gujarat Vigha conversions differ: Saurashtra Vigha = 16 Gunthas, Gujarat Standard Vigha = 20 Gunthas, and Gaekwad Vigha = 24 Gunthas [Revenue Dept 2026].

Where can grape growers check live daily mandi prices in Nashik, Sangli, or Vijayapura?

Check official daily wholesale arrivals and modal rates on agmarknet.gov.in and enam.gov.in for Pimpalgaon, Lasalgaon, Dindori, Tasgaon, Solapur, and Vijayapura mandis.
